amendments_relevant: Chapter 8 (interior finishes): only Section 808.1.1.3 (drop-out ceiling panels) is added, so Section 803.9 of the 2024 IBC (HDPE and polypropylene) applies unamended.
Table 1004.5: business areas changed to '150 gross / 100 net', footnote c: use whichever gives the greater occupant load.
Chapter 11: Sections 1101.1, 1101.2, 1107 and 1112 amended; Section 1110.2.4 (5 percent of compartments wheelchair accessible) unamended.
Section 2902: 2902.3.2 and 2902.7 amended, 2902.8 (all-gender multi-user toilet rooms) and 2902.10 (drive-in facilities) added; Table 2902.1 unamended.

fixtures.city_amends_note: The counts are unchanged, but Denver moves them: it deletes Section 403 of the plumbing code and applies Section 2902 and Table 2902.1 of its building code (2024 IBC), whose rows for business, restaurants and educational facilities read the same as the state table. Denver adds one rule of its own, Section 2902.8, for all-gender multi-user rooms (see amendment). The state pack's worked examples stand.

amendment.text: In an all-gender multi-user toilet room, each toilet must be in its own compartment that runs from floor to ceiling (or starts no more than 4.5 inches above the floor and reaches at least 96 inches), with no sightlines and a lockable door; door undercut at most 0.5 inch. A urinal is allowed only inside a toilet compartment and does not count toward the required fixtures.
amendment.quote: [P] 2902.8 All-gender multi-user toilet rooms. Where all-gender multi-user toilet rooms are provided, they shall be in accordance with this section. Water closets shall each be provided in individual compartments. Compartments shall be permitted to include walls, partitions and doors and shall begin at the floor and extend to the finished ceiling, have no sightlines when the door is in the closed position and have a lockable door in accordance with Section 2902.3.6.3. A urinal shall be permitted only within a water closet compartment; such urinal shall not contribute towards the total number of required plumbing fixtures. Exceptions: 1. Compartment door undercuts shall be permitted to be not more than 0.5 inches. (13 mm). 2. Air transfer grills at the entrance side of a compartment shall be allowed where they are provided at a height not less than 80 inches (2134 mm). 3. Partial-height toilet compartments are permitted where they begin at a height not more than 4.5 inches (114 mm) and extend to a height not less than 96 inches (2438 mm) above the finished floor surface.

fixtures.table_quote: [Table 2902.1 as shown on UpCodes' Denver copy:] Restaurants, banquet halls and food courts(d): water closets 1 per 75 male, 1 per 75 female. Business: 1 per 25 for the first 50 and 1 per 50 for the remainder exceeding 50. Educational facilities: 1 per 50. [2902.1.1:] To determine the occupant load of each sex, the total occupant load shall be divided in half. [...] Where multiple-user facilities are designed to serve all genders, the minimum fixture count shall be calculated 100 percent, based on total occupant load. [2902.2 exceptions:] Separate toilet facilities shall not be required in structures or tenant spaces with a total occupant load, including both employees and customers, of 15 or fewer. [...] in business occupancies in which the maximum occupant load is 25 or fewer. [IPC 424.2, Denver copy:] In each bathroom or toilet room, urinals shall not be substituted for more than 67 percent of the required water closets for males according to Table 403.1 in assembly and educational occupancies. Urinals shall not be substituted for more than 50 percent of the required water closets for males according to Table 403.1 in all other occupancies.
fixtures.confidence_note: Denver's amendments were read in the city's own code PDF. The unamended table and sections of the 2024 IBC and IPC were read on UpCodes' copy of the Denver code (the ICC's site blocks automated access).

Single-user rooms: the adopted 2024 IBC Section 2902.1.2 requires them to be identified as available to all persons regardless of sex, the same as the state rule; no further Denver amendment on signs was found in the 2025 code.

page.meta: Commercial bathroom partitions delivered to Denver job sites. Price your restroom, pick a material and see the Denver building rules that apply.
page.lead: Commercial bathroom partitions for Denver offices, schools, breweries and airport-area warehouses, shipped by freight to your job site.
page.fire_bullet: - **Fire safety:** Denver's building rules require solid plastic (HDPE) used as an interior finish to pass a room fire test. Ask for the fire-rated version.
page.stall_bullet: - **How many stalls:** Denver's building rules set the number of toilets and urinals by how many people use the building. The table below shows what that means.
page.state_extra_bullet: - **Denver extras:** in very large restrooms, Denver's building rules ask for 5% of the stalls to be wheelchair accessible, where federal law asks for at least one. The city's rules also state that meeting them does not assure that a design meets federal access law.
page.restroom_bullet: - **Single-user and all-gender restrooms:** a one-person restroom must be marked as open to everyone. Denver allows a shared all-gender room and sets its own stall rule for it: every toilet sits in a compartment with a lockable door and no sightlines, running from the floor to the ceiling, or starting no more than 4.5 inches above the floor and reaching at least 8 feet. The gap under the door can be half an inch at most. A urinal is allowed in such a room only inside a toilet compartment, and it doesn't count toward the required number. In buildings owned by the state, a state college, a county or a city, a new building or a renovated restroom must include an all-gender restroom; K-12 schools are outside that law. Colorado's civil rights rules allow separate men's and women's rooms and require that people may use the one that matches their gender identity.
page.permit_bullet: - **Permits:** Denver requires a permit to alter or remodel a building and lists the work that needs none. The list covers repairs, painting, tiling, floor coverings, countertops and cabinets, and movable partitions no taller than 5 feet 9 inches. It doesn't name toilet partitions fixed to the floor or wall, so ask Denver Community Planning and Development (720-865-2700) whether your replacement needs one. You don't need a permit to buy partitions.
page.stalls_intro: Denver's building rules count toilets by a building's capacity: the most people it is designed to hold at one time, worked out from its floor area. It isn't the number of staff or of visitors in a day. Half are counted as men and half as women, and every toilet needs a stall. Urinals are optional: in each men's room they may replace up to half of the toilets in an office and up to two thirds in a restaurant or school, and each urinal then needs a screen.
page.stalls_after: These are Denver's minimums for the whole building. An office that holds 25 people or fewer, or any space that holds 15 or fewer, does not need separate men's and women's rooms. A shared all-gender room is counted on everyone in the building instead of half. A restaurant's seasonal outdoor seating counts toward the number of people. Public school projects are reviewed and permitted by the state, not the city, and the state's counts are the same.
page.capacity: To find your building's capacity, Denver's building rules count an office at one person per 150 square feet of the whole floor or one per 100 square feet of the office space itself, whichever gives more people, a restaurant dining room at one per 15 square feet and a classroom at one per 20. Your architect or Denver Community Planning and Development sets the final number.
page.install_rule: Denver requires a Denver-issued building contractor license (Class A, B or a specialty class, backed by a supervisor certificate) to pull permits, and it doesn't accept licenses from other states or counties. Colorado doesn't license general or specialty contractors at the state level. You don't need a permit to buy partitions.
page.faq_install_extra: A contractor who pulls a permit in Denver needs a Denver contractor license.
page.public_jobs_bullet: - **Public jobs:** Colorado's wage law for public jobs covers state agency projects of $500,000 or more without federal money, at rates the state takes from the federal wage tables for the county. For a carpenter on building work in Denver County the federal rate is $21.09 an hour plus $6.31 in benefits. Denver has its own wage rule for city contracts of $2,000 or more: the city's schedule sets $23.09 an hour plus $6.31 in benefits for a carpenter.
page.sales_tax_bullet: - **Sales tax:** 9.15% in Denver: 5.15% city, 2.9% state, 1% transit district and 0.1% cultural district. Denver collects its own 5.15% under its own tax rules.
page.tax_install_bullet: - **Tax on installation:** installation labor listed separately on the bid, invoice or contract isn't taxed. A contractor who supplies and installs building materials pays Denver's tax on those materials instead of charging it to the customer, and Denver gives no exemption for materials on government, religious or charity projects.
page.tax_ship_bullet: - **Buying without installation:** partitions shipped to Denver are taxable. Denver taxes freight that the seller charges or arranges as part of the price; the state taxes it unless it is an optional charge shown on its own line. If the seller doesn't collect the tax, the buyer owes it as use tax.
page.tax_confirm: your accountant, the Denver Treasury Division or the Colorado Department of Revenue
page.buyers_extra: - **Breweries, music venues and stadiums:** HDPE or phenolic where crowds and nightly washdown are hard on stalls, stainless steel in premium public restrooms.

page.official_names: - The rules by their official names: 2010 ADA Standards for Accessible Design; 2025 Denver Building Code, 2nd Printing (November 2025), adopted June 13, 2025 under Denver Revised Municipal Code section 10-16 and in force for projects first submitted after December 31, 2025: Denver Commercial Building Code (2024 International Building Code with Denver amendments; Sections 130.3, 803.9, 1110.2.4, 2902 and 2902.8, Tables 1004.5 and 2902.1) and Denver Plumbing Code (2024 International Plumbing Code with Denver amendments; Sections 405.3.4, 405.3.5 and 424.2); ICC A117.1-2017; Colorado Plumbing Code, 3 CCR 720-1 (state minimum); C.R.S. 9-5.7-103 for restrooms in public-entity buildings; NFPA 286 for HDPE.
notes: To confirm by phone before launch: whether a like-for-like replacement of anchored toilet partitions needs a Denver permit (Community Planning and Development, 720-865-2700, planreview@denvergov.org).

Denver's all-gender rule means standard partitions (open at floor and top) don't meet the city's rule for a shared all-gender room: floor-to-ceiling or 4.5 in to 96 in compartments are needed there. Worth a product link once the catalogue has a full-height privacy line.

Unamended sections of the 2024 International Building Code and International Plumbing Code (fixture table, urinal rule, HDPE fire test, occupant load table, accessible stall count) were read on UpCodes' copy of the Denver code: check once on codes.iccsafe.org in a browser.

Sales tax: news reports say Front Range Passenger Rail District Ballot Issue 7A (a new 0.333% sales and use tax) was passing in unofficial returns of the November 3, 2026 election. Confirm with the Colorado Department of Revenue whether Denver addresses are in the district and when collection starts, then update the 9.15% rate.

Sales tax: the Colorado Department of Revenue's rate publication DR 1002 could not be opened (403); the rate and its parts come from Denver Treasury's own table. Denver's guide for contractors still prints the old 4.81% city rate; the no-exemption statement was taken from it and from Treasury Tax Rule 005.

Whether toilet partitions sold with installation are 'construction materials' (the installer pays the tax) or 'completed units' (the seller collects tax on the goods, not on separately stated installation) under Denver's Treasury Tax Rule 005 is not stated: ask Denver Treasury's audit unit, 720-913-9955, constructiontaxinfo@denvergov.org.

The asterisk on the city's $23.09 carpenter rate is not explained in the Denver schedule: confirm with the Auditor's Office (Denver Labor) and recheck the schedule, which is reissued several times a year.

News reports from 2016 to 2018 describe a Denver rule that made existing single-stall restrooms switch to gender-neutral signs by spring 2018; it was not found in the 2025 code and is not on the page. Confirm with Community Planning and Development whether it still applies to existing buildings.
Denver doesn't expect to adopt a newer code edition before late 2027 (Building Permit Policy 25-DCBC 131.2): recheck the codes then.
